claims.reason: The grade letter B is editorial and was not checked. Supported: a systematic measurement of routers from named purchase channels and public communities (a convenience sample, no claim of market coverage). Narrower than the source: the paper is not only one measurement study; it also has two poisoning studies and builds a research proxy to evaluate three defences. That the sample is not representative is not stated in the abstract; it is an inference from the sampling description.

quotes.text: evaluate three deployable client-side defenses: a fail-closed policy gate, response-side anomaly screening, and append-only transparency logging

claims.reason: The abstract names three automated client-side defences and adaptive evasion variants, but reports no results and does not mention human review of commands. Full text would be needed to see whether human review is evaluated or its limits discussed.

scope_gaps.note: The abstract gives no comparison of risk between paid and free routers; it only shows that a paid router was among the malicious ones.
The sample came from named channels (Taobao, Xianyu, Shopify-hosted storefronts for paid; public communities for free), not a census of the market.
Abstract does not state where the malicious code was injected (responses vs request payloads); 'touching' canary credentials is the abstract's wording for access.
The paper includes two poisoning studies and a defence evaluation with a research proxy, beyond a single measurement study.
Abstract reports no results for any defence and does not test restricting automatic execution; the advice rests on the injection finding and is a practical inference.
Source covers third-party routers; official or direct provider connections are outside what was measured.
Personal-data law is outside the paper's subject.
Human review of commands is not among the defences named in the abstract.

notes: Only one source (arXiv abstract page 2604.08407, snapshot aff92e5a2fd5f64c.txt) is cited and the snapshot holds the abstract page only (main region 4689 of 5099 chars), no full text; no packet warnings.
